headline: Data-driven models probe nonlinear fitness landscapes and population dynamics
label: Data Driven Models Of Evolution
summary: Interpretability and structure-learning tools are now applied to population genetic and fitness-landscape data, testing what learned models actually represent.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of data-driven models to recover interpretable structure in evolutionary and fitness data, with emphasis on what the model representation encodes. A preprint links convolutional neural network features in population genetics to classical summary statistics such as heterozygosity and linkage disequilibrium, using SHAP attribution to connect learned features to those quantities. A second preprint tests whether the choice of power transform changes inferred nonlinearity in the GFP random mutagenesis fitness landscape, reporting that Box-Cox reduces local pairwise epistasis by 19.4%. A published study extends weak-form sparse identification (WSINDy) to structured population models with heterogeneous dynamics and boundary processes. What is new across these items is the explicit treatment of model outputs and parameterization choices as objects of biological interrogation, rather than as predictive endpoints alone.
